hints.text: Hunt for two numbers that multiply to $-6$ and add to $-1$. One must be negative!

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Easier one: $x^2 + 5x + 6$ needs two numbers multiplying to $6$ and adding to $5$ — that is $2$ and $3$. Yours needs a NEGATIVE product.
Try the pairs: $-6$ and $1$ add to $-5$. What about $-3$ and $2$?

explanation: Need two numbers with product $-6$ and sum $-1$.
A negative product means one number is negative.
The pair $-3$ and $+2$ works: product $-6$, sum $-1$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sign detective
steps: Product negative → the two numbers have DIFFERENT signs.
Sum negative → the bigger-sized number wears the minus.
Pairs for 6: (1, 6) and (2, 3). Only −3 and +2 sum to −1.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check by expanding
steps: Combine: x² − x − 6. It matches the original, so the factoring is right.
